name: Decay Card
description: Image card rendered in WebGL that follows the cursor with tilt and travel, and tears apart into noise-driven displacement when the pointer moves fast, then recovers smoothly.
contents: Single card sized by width and height, drawn on a WebGL2 canvas with a noise distortion shader
Optional children overlay at the bottom of the card, in white text
Plain img fallback when WebGL2 or the image texture fails
behavior: Card drifts and rotates toward the cursor with eased follow, either across the whole window or only while hovered
Fast cursor movement raises a decay level that displaces the image with turbulence noise, strongest at the edges, then recovers
Idle noise slowly eats at the card rim even without interaction
Optional chromatic split, grayscale, flowing noise and rounded corners
Render loop pauses when the card is offscreen or settled
Prefers-reduced-motion disables movement, tilt and flow
editableByProps: Image, card size, corner radius, grayscale and chromatic split
Decay strength, cursor sensitivity, hover decay, recovery speed, grain size, detail, noise pattern seed, idle erosion and flow
Cursor travel distance, tilt angle and whether the cursor tracked is the whole window or the card only
Overlay content through children, extra classes and inline style

needsCodeEdit.change: Change the overlay text color or position
Change the aspect ratio the shader assumes for the image crop
needsCodeEdit.where: sampleImage function in the FRAGMENT shader
follow constant inside the frame function

fixed: Needs WebGL2, otherwise it shows a static image without effects
Listens to window pointermove for the whole lifetime, even in card scope
Image must allow cross-origin loading (crossOrigin anonymous), otherwise the fallback img shows
Canvas bleeds 24 percent beyond the card box, so surrounding space should not clip overflow
Card is flex-none with a pixel width and height, not responsive by itself; wrap or pass smaller width and height on small screens
Window scope follows cursor position across the viewport, so it has no effect on touch devices without pointer movement
